After any number of receive calls, the contract balance minus depositsCount must be zero (since each deposit of X ether increments depositsCount by 1), but the mutant increments depositsCount by 2, so after at least one deposit the invariant balance >= depositsCount becomes balance < depositsCount (or more precisely balance - depositsCount is negative, failing the invariant that balance equals depositsCount).

After any number of calls to receive(), depositsCount must equal the number of successful deposits (i.e., the balance of the contract); the mutant fails after the first deposit since depositsCount remains 0.

For any sequence of payable receive calls, depositsCount must be strictly greater than zero after at least one successful deposit; the mutant leaves depositsCount at 0, violating the invariant that depositsCount reflects successful deposits.

After any successful deposit via receive, the contract's balance must be at least depositsCount, because each deposit increments depositsCount by 1 and adds at least 1 wei; the mutant leaves depositsCount unchanged, so after a deposit of value > 1e18 the balance exceeds depositsCount but a subsequent zero-value deposit fails the overflow check, yet with a 1 wei deposit the invariant still holds.

After any sequence of calls, depositsCount must equal the number of times receive() completed successfully (i.e., the number of deposits that did not revert); the mutant breaks this by never incrementing depositsCount, so after one successful deposit the counts diverge and a subsequent deposit with a different amount still leaves depositsCount stuck at 0.

For any sequence of deposits, depositsCount must be at least address(c).balance in wei, because each deposit adds at least 1 wei and increments depositsCount by 1; the mutant never increments depositsCount, so after depositing more than 1 wei, depositsCount < address(c).balance.

After any sequence of receives, depositsCount is at least the initial value (0); the buggy version overflows and wraps depositsCount to 0, making depositsCount less than the initial value.

After any sequence of receive calls, address(c).balance must equal depositsCount if each call sends exactly 1 wei; the buggy version overflows depositsCount, breaking equality while balance correctly accumulates.
